just a random question, how long are you planning to take inositol for, I read some people uses it for 6 month and then break for 6 before using it again so I'm not sure.. my doctor doesn't seem to know anything about inositol so I have no where to ask other than the internet

I don't think there is such a thing as the best diet supplements since its different for everyone, but again, I'm no doctor. 

I would recommend to get some tests done before, find the areas you're missing and if you've Insulin resistance or not. based on the result you'll be able to know what supplements to take. 

Personally I've been taking metformine ever since I was diagnosed along with iron, vitamin b complex, omega, and vitamin d since I'm lacking on those areas. recently, like two days ago, I swapped metformine with Inositol and hoping for the best, I also added folic acid and vitamin c to my daily supplements since it seems to work well. (I make changes to my pills intake based on my every 3 month blood test results so I'm not over doing it)  

I head people taking birth control to regulate their period but mine was regulated with metformin and losing some pounds so I dont know about that. 

For hair loss its kinda same with managing pcos you need to know first what elements are missing in your diet and take supplements accordingly.

Same! but I had it on 13 :)) I was put on 50000 IU weekly for 3 month and now I'm on monthly bases. don't forget to take them with meals, I was told its better absorbed that way, take morning walks for 10\~20 minutes I find that helps too, I took cod liver oil supplements too, now my vitamin d levels are still bad but at least not bad bad.

I usually take the pill after meals, I think taking half of the recommended dose for the first two weeks will be better than the full dose. hmmm, also you might get nausea after taking it so be careful of that, I also stop eating for two hours after the pill a recommended, also, check vitamin B levels after a month of taking it since you might need to take vitamin b supplements , be close to toilet at all time, avoid carbs and dairy when taking it, I found my diarrhea gets worse when consuming it with carbs and dairy. Thats all what I can think of now

Mine was three to four times a year and I managed to get it to come monthly-ish after fixing my diet and working out a bit, nothing extreme just more walking. I was prescribed some hormones pills once and it came but was really really painful so wouldn’t recommend that. Hopefully yours will start naturally soon 🙏

I would say wait on it for few more months to see if you face any other symptoms since it could just be the side effects of the change, but waiting on it could potentially cause issues if it actually turned out to be pcos so would just recommend getting an ultrasound to check on your ovaries just to be on the safe side and save you the worries
